correctness.rationale: Integrating the three coordinate derivatives under an invariant compactly supported measure gives \(\langle y^2\rangle=m\langle y\rangle\), \(\langle xy\rangle=-a\langle z^2\rangle\), and \(\langle x^2\rangle=(ac/b)\langle z^2\rangle\). Variance nonnegativity yields \(0\le\langle y\rangle\le m\). Cauchy--Schwarz applied to \(\langle xy\rangle\), followed by the exact \(x^2/z^2\) ratio, gives the sharp outer bounds. Equality forces zero variance in \(y\), after which support invariance reduces the support to the explicitly solved equilibria. Fresh symbolic simplification independently reproduced \(ac/b=1\), \(c/(ab)=4\), and \(c^2/b^2=4\) at the published coefficients.
risks: The theorem is conditional on compact support and does not prove existence/ergodicity of the numerically displayed chaotic attractor.

final_claim: For the printed amplitude-controlled SL8I flow \(\dot x=my-y^2,\ \dot y=az^2+xy,\ \dot z=bx^2+cxy\) with positive parameters, every compactly supported invariant probability measure obeys the exact stationary identities and the sharp second-moment envelope stated in the package, with complete equality classification; at \((a,b,c)=(1/2,3/5,6/5)\), every non-equilibrium ergodic compact recurrent state has \(\operatorname{RMS}(y)<m\) and \(\operatorname{RMS}(x)=\operatorname{RMS}(z)<2m\).
limitations: No existence, uniqueness, or physicality theorem for chaotic measures.
